title: What does one change force Docker to rebuild?
description: Choose a Dockerfile structure and a changed input. The trace uses illustrative timings and sizes to expose cache invalidation and final-image boundaries; measure your own build before setting targets.

changes.label: Application source changes
changes.detail: A frequently edited source file changes while dependency manifests and base images stay fixed.

changes.label: Dependency lockfile changes
changes.detail: The exact dependency graph changes, so install layers and their dependents need new outputs.

changes.label: Base image digest changes
changes.detail: The builder and runtime bases are refreshed to new immutable image content.

designs.label: Copy everything, then install
designs.detail: One stage copies the whole context before dependency installation and ships the build toolchain.
buildOnlyContents: none; every build artifact remains in the runtime image
designs.recommendation: A source edit invalidates expensive dependency work and the runtime image carries build-only material

layers.label: Resolve one base image
layers.detail: The same filesystem becomes both the build environment and the runtime base.

layers.label: Copy the entire build context
layers.detail: Source, manifests, tests, and any files not excluded by .dockerignore enter one layer.

layers.label: Install all dependencies
layers.detail: Changing any earlier copied file changes this layer's parent and makes the install run again.

layers.label: Compile the application
layers.detail: Build tools and intermediate output stay in the same image history used at runtime.

layers.label: Set runtime metadata
layers.detail: The final command and image configuration follow the mutable build steps.

designs.label: Cache-aware multi-stage build
designs.detail: Stable manifests precede source, and the runtime stage copies only production dependencies and compiled output.
designs.recommendation: Frequent source edits preserve dependency layers while multi-stage copying keeps build tools out of the final image

layers.label: Resolve builder base
layers.detail: The builder provides the complete toolchain but does not become the final runtime image.

layers.label: Copy dependency manifests
layers.detail: The lockfile is isolated from frequently changing application source.

layers.label: Install build dependencies
layers.detail: A BuildKit cache mount can reuse downloaded packages even when the install instruction runs again.

layers.label: Copy application source
layers.detail: Source changes begin invalidation here instead of before dependency installation.

layers.label: Compile application output
layers.detail: The build stage produces the files required by the runtime stage.

layers.label: Resolve minimal runtime base
layers.detail: The runtime stage begins from a separate image without the builder toolchain.

layers.label: Install production dependencies
layers.detail: Only packages needed by the running process enter the final image.

layers.label: Copy compiled output
layers.detail: The runtime stage receives selected artifacts from the builder stage.

layers.label: Set user and command
layers.detail: The image records an unprivileged runtime user and the application command.
